title: Austere Systems Ltd - 544505 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Austere Systems H1 FY27 revenue rose 9.12% to INR11.29 crore, while net profit margin fell to 14.75% after a INR44 lakh legal provision.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR11.29 crore against INR10.34 crore a year earlier (+9.12%), and total income grew 13% to INR11.97 crore. EBITDA was INR2.99 crore at a 25.01% margin, described as broadly in line with prior periods despite a provision of about INR44 lakh against a pending legal case. Net profit was INR1.77 crore (14.75% margin), reduced by that provision and by higher depreciation on assets added late in FY26. Management highlighted new wins (HDFC Bank MIS work orders worth INR1.87 crore, two HARTRON work orders), new subsidiaries and partnerships for overseas and enterprise and AI work, and said other income rose on IPO-proceed interest that it does not expect to recur.

segments.name: Services (IT services, consulting, implementation)
segments.commentary: Management said 80-90% of revenue comes from services, delivered on milestone billing; the company describes itself as a services company. Product/SaaS revenue share was not quantified for H1.

segments.name: Urban digital governance (Dial 11-UrbanSphere)
segments.commentary: Named as the strongest growth area for H2; platform is being rolled out to more municipal corporations, with GIS and AI modules being added. Two HARTRON orders extend the model to another corporation and a police-department analytics solution.

segments.name: Enterprise / corporate (Austere Next Pvt Ltd, 51% held)
segments.commentary: Set up for SAP, ServiceNow, Oracle and Salesforce work with an AI practice; AI lab being set up in Gurugram. No revenue contribution disclosed yet.

segments.name: Overseas (Austere Systems LLC, Delaware)
segments.commentary: Wholly owned US subsidiary for IT consulting; management says client pipeline is strong but gave no figures. Sales also active in Europe.

guidance_outlook: Management does not provide forward-looking revenue guidance and does not publish a consolidated order book.
Stated intent to maintain EBITDA margin around current levels through productivity, utilisation and cost discipline.
Stated intent to keep growing revenue at the recent pace over 3-5 years; no numeric targets given.
Health and education sectors named as priority verticals for investment.
IPO proceeds to be deployed into growth; management said no further fundraising is planned.
capex_capacity: Assets added late in FY26 carry a full six-month depreciation charge in H1 FY27, raising depreciation.
AI lab being set up at Gurugram premises.
Delaware office for Austere Systems LLC opened recently; Austere Next incorporated with 51% holding.
Partner in Neural Nexis AI LLP to build AI-led services.
No quantified capex plan or capacity utilisation figures were given on the call.
demand_pricing: Retention of 80-90% of existing clients for repeat business, per management.
Revenue split of about 40% government and 60% corporate (management said 40:60 ratio between government and corporate).
Government payments are milestone-linked; management cited administrative delays from bureaucratic transfers as the main cause of slippage.
Receivables up about 6% YoY against 9% revenue growth; management is tracking aging and splitting milestones to speed collection.
Management said it cannot disclose the H1 growth drivers by customer or the payment cycle by client type.
Competition positioned on bespoke, client-need-led solutions and AI used where it fits, not pushed; no pricing data given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net profit margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a prudential provision of about INR44 lakh against a pending legal case, plus higher depreciation on late-FY26 asset additions carrying a full six-month charge. EBITDA margin was said to be broadly similar to the prior cycle.

qa_highlights.question: Is fundraising or bank debt planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the company is cash-rich and debt-free with IPO proceeds available, and will use those rather than raise further funds. Utilisation details were referred to SEBI disclosures.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not publish a consolidated order book or pipeline. It announces significant orders by press release only; HDFC Bank (INR1.87 crore) and two HARTRON orders were cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between services and products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80-90% of revenue is services; in-house products are delivered as services on milestone billing. The split is expected to stay similar, with product sales to be announced separately.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly interest earned on IPO proceeds parked in short-term deposits. Management said this is not recurring because the proceeds will be deployed into growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is expected from the overseas and Austere Next businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no numbers. It said the US entity gives local presence that improves preference for overseas bids, and Austere Next focuses on enterprise platforms (SAP, ServiceNow, Oracle, Salesforce).

risks_watch: Profit margin pressure from the INR44 lakh legal provision and higher depreciation; check whether the provision moves and whether depreciation stays elevated.
Receivables growing faster than revenue are not yet fully resolved, and government payments can be delayed by bureaucratic transfers.
Revenue concentration in government clients, and the ability to roll out the UrbanSphere model across more corporations and states.
Early-stage overseas and AI initiatives (Delaware LLC, Austere Next, Neural Nexis) have no disclosed revenue; watch for first-order announcements.
Other income will fall as IPO proceeds are deployed, which will lower reported profit before tax.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on retention and long-term direction but evasive on quantitative detail. It declined to disclose order book, pipeline, client names, payment cycles and forward revenue, and answered several questions only partly, including the revenue split and government payment timing.
